title: the AT status machine has no inverse for to-write, and the forward step can refuse every commit in the repository
body:
**THE AT STATUS MACHINE HAS A ONE-WAY DOOR, AND THE STEP THROUGH IT CAN REFUSE EVERY COMMIT IN THE REPOSITORY.**

`intent at` offers `green`, `red`, `na`, `new` and `edit`. **NO SPELLING RETURNS A ROW TO `to-write`.** Driven on `da5919e8`: `at set` is not a subcommand, and `at --help` lists the five above and nothing else.

That asymmetry is harmless on its own. It is not harmless combined with the lint rule beside it.

## The two states differ in blast radius, not just in colour

| row state | cited file absent | consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `to-write` | EXEMPT -- `absent_at_check.sh:107`, "the normal state" | nothing |
| `red` | a LIVE `absent_at` finding | **the pre-commit gate refuses EVERY node's commit** |

So `to-write -> red` on a row whose citation does not exist yet converts a quiet, legal row into a repository-wide block, **and there is no verb to step back.**

## The live instance, armed today

`ST0056 AT-00.2` is `to-write` and cites `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/tests/fleet_corpus_ingest.rs`, **which has never existed**. It is legal right now and nothing is broken this minute.

It became live again at `a19d8b5c`, when `AC-00.2` was reinstated on hv's ruling -- so the requirement it guards is now IN the 3.0.1 cut, which is exactly the condition under which somebody will reach for `at red` to make the row honest.

**AND THE ROW'S OWN NOTE INSTRUCTED THE TRAP.** It read `red-first against the canary tree` -- correct as a testing discipline, and the precise action that detonates this. Rewritten in place to carry the warning.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed in passing

**The warning previously existed only in the header of a SIBLING file**, `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/fleet_corpus_conservation.sh`, which records `AT-10.5` going through this same door. cc found it only because they had read that header this morning for an unrelated reason. **A fact whose one home is a file nobody opens on the way to the operation is not a control.** It has been moved onto `AT-00.2`'s own row, which is the surface an operator touches -- but that is one row, by hand, and the door stays open for every other `to-write` row in the estate.

## Dispositions, none taken

1. **Give the machine an inverse** -- a spelling that returns a row to `to-write`. Makes the door two-way; the transition stops being a trap.
2. **Guard the forward step** -- `at red` refuses, or warns, when the cited file is absent, naming the consequence. Narrower, and it defends every row rather than one.
3. **Neither** -- accept it and rely on notes. This is the status quo, and it is what produced the one-row-at-a-time fix above.

Found by cc, 2026-09-05, flagged rather than claimed. Filed by vc.
